sapience-retrieve.sh was confirmed to be byte-for-byte API-compatible with memory-retrieve.sh (same 3-positional-arg signature, same <memory-context> envelope, same deployed path), making the 25-site Part C cleanup a mechanical rename rather than a logic rewrite.

Part B's six-sub-mode deletion (report/purge/merge/compress/refine/gc) is not a clean six-section removal: the Scoring Engine's composite-score and health_score formulas must be retained because the surviving 'auto' sub-mode still consumes them for its own health_score recalculation, while only the Health Report Template and Maintenance Candidate Classification table are safe to delete outright. Flagged in the research report for the plan phase.

Plan-phase live probe settled the Part C2 keep-vs-replace sub-decision with evidence instead of judgment: an unfiltered mcp__sapience__sapience_search returned a KO whose provenance carries [repo:nvim] alongside untagged KOs, proving the repo tag narrows only reads that request the source= filter. A tagged write is therefore strictly more reachable than an untagged one, so replacing the untagged sapience_wrapup call rather than keeping both halves permanent unreviewed write volume at zero reachability cost.

Re-derivation at plan time found the declared file_scope materially narrower than the work the task requires: the 25 extension Stage 4a call sites (confirmed live, 25 of 25 still invoking the retired retrieval script), memory/EXTENSION.md, memory/commands/distill.md, the four deleted submode pattern files, core/manifest.json and roughly a dozen prose-reference files are all absent from it. specs/.gate-lock (the global mutex serializing run-all.sh / verify-deploy.sh gate 8) is held by a DEAD process: owner file names session=verify-deploy-gate8-2227510, pid=2227797, claimed_at=1794349745; 'ps -p 2227797' returns nothing (process does not exist), but stale_sec=1800 means the lock will not be auto-reclaimed until roughly 30 minutes after the original claim. At least 5 other sibling run-all.sh invocations (pids 2710301, 2840495, 3335136, 3823918, 3910385, all with --fail-on-new) are queued waiting behind this same dead lock as of this observation, confirming this is a repo-wide, multi-session contention problem, not specific to this task. Did NOT attempt to clear the lock directory myself (specs/.gate-lock) since it is shared infrastructure and another concurrent session's assumptions could depend on it; per the territory contract this is reported rather than worked around. Consequence for this task: verify-deploy.sh's full run reported FAIL at gate 8 (run-all.sh, undiscoverable/failing suites due to the same lock wait) and gate 10 (validate-state.sh --deep, 60s timeout) during a period of heavy concurrent load; both were independently re-verified clean when run standalone outside the contended window (validate-state.sh --deep: 20 passed, 0 failed via the deployed path; the three test suites this task's own Phase 4 edits touch -- test-orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh, test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh, test-script-inventory.sh -- all pass cleanly run individually).

Phase 7's Part C2 write-verification step (write a real, bounded note set via sapience-remember.sh and confirm written >= 1) could NOT be completed: every attempt to POST a coherent, real-English-sentence note to /ingest-kos hangs with ZERO bytes received, confirmed up to a 270-second curl timeout (tried subjects/values of varying length from ~50 to ~700 chars, all hung). By contrast, short nonsense/throwaway content (e.g. 'diagnostic retry 5', a string of repeated letters) reliably gets a FAST response (gated=1 or written=0) within ~1 second. This pattern was reproduced consistently (4+ real attempts, plus manual curl diagnostics bypassing the script entirely) and is not attributable to anything this task changed -- sapience-remember.sh's and sapience-retrieve.sh's actual request-building/curl logic is UNCHANGED by this task (only header comments were edited in Phase 4). Confirmed NOT a general connectivity problem: a plain GET to the host returns 200 in <1s, sapience-retrieve.sh reads succeed normally throughout this dispatch, and a deliberately noisy/low-quality write reaches the server and gets gated/rejected fast. This looks like a genuine Sapience-service-side issue specific to real-content POST /ingest-kos requests (possibly a WAF/content-filter silently dropping the connection, or an expensive server-side path that never returns) -- an infrastructure observation about the external vault, not a defect in this task's deliverable. The script's own designed degrade behavior (its internal --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 ceiling, fail loud and fast, log-and-step-over) was independently confirmed correct via the dry-run, the forced-bogus-host failure, and by the fact that every one of these hangs was observed via a manual curl bypassing the script's own tight timeout -- the actual deployed script itself never hangs beyond its designed ~8s ceiling. The written>=1 success case and the full write-verification loop (point 2 of Phase 7's write-verification bullet, confirming a later dispatch's sapience-retrieve.sh sees this task's own note) could not be positively demonstrated in this dispatch as a result. Recommend an operator investigate POST /ingest-kos directly (outside this task) before relying on the tagged-write loop Phase 6 just wired.
